title: Task statuses after a failure
prompt: Three of the nightly job's tasks are quality gates that raise an error when the data is wrong. Finish `solve(shipments, shipment_events, deliveries)` so it runs the tasks in order and returns one row per task: its name in `task` and its `status`.
rules: `failed`: the task ran and raised an error. `skipped`: a task it needs is `failed` or `skipped`, so it doesn't run at all. `ok`: it ran without an error.
A failure doesn't stop tasks that don't need the failed one: they still run. Return all five tasks.
hints: `run_order(deps)` gives an order where every task comes after the tasks it needs.
Before running a task, look at the statuses of the tasks it needs. Any that isn't `ok` means `skipped`.
Wrap the call in `try` / `except Exception` and set `failed` in the `except`.
